findings.evidence: `grep -n hA TauCeti/Analysis/Semigroups/Generation/Yosida.lean` → the hypothesis is consumed only at line 86; lines 97, 176, 190 just forward it. Roadmap OneParameterSemigroups/README.md: "theorem hilleYosida_generation (A : DenseLinearOperator X) (hρ : ∀ l : ℝ, ω < l → l ∈ resolventSet A) (hbound : ...)" and "⚠ Both are genuinely open / build-here, via the same Yosida approximation".
findings.fix: Replace `(hA : IsMDissipative A)` by `(hres : ‖LinearPMap.resolvent A lambda‖ ≤ lambda⁻¹)` in all four declarations (the wrappers at 195/203/210/219 then carry `hres` instead of `hA` unchanged), and recover the m-dissipative case at the call site from `hA.norm_resolvent_le hlambda`, added by this same PR in Dissipative/Basic.lean. The proofs go through verbatim: `norm_smul_resolvent_le_one` becomes `gcongr; exact hres`, and 90/138/181 already route through it. Note `yosidaApproximation_apply_eq_smul_apply_resolvent` (71) already keys on the weak hypothesis `lambda ∈ LinearPMap.resolventSet A`, so the file is internally inconsistent about this.
findings.issue: `norm_smul_resolvent_le_one` (79), `norm_yosidaApproximation_le` (90), `norm_exp_yosidaApproximation_le_one` (138) and `yosidaSemigroup` (181) all assume `hA : IsMDissipative A`, but the only mathematical use of `hA` in the whole file is line 86, `exact hA.norm_resolvent_le hlambda`. The hypothesis is strictly stronger than what the proofs need, and it is the Lumer–Phillips hypothesis set, not the Hille–Yosida one the PR claims to advance: the roadmap's Hille–Yosida milestone reads `(ω,∞) ⊆ ρ(A)` plus `‖R(λ,A)ⁿ‖ ≤ M/(λ−ω)ⁿ` with no dissipativity anywhere, so as stated none of this API applies under those hypotheses and the contraction estimate would have to be re-derived.

findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Algebra/Exponential.lean:446-472 (`variable [NormedRing 𝔸] [NormedAlgebra 𝕂 𝔸]`, `expSeries_radius_eq_top`, `norm_expSeries_summable'`) and Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Ring/Basic.lean:425 (`norm_pow_le'` for a seminormed ring); the only operator-specific step in the PR's proof is `ContinuousLinearMap.norm_id_le`, i.e. `‖1‖ ≤ 1`.
findings.fix: State both over `{𝔸 : Type*} [NormedRing 𝔸] [NormedAlgebra ℝ 𝔸]`: `exp_add_of_commute [CompleteSpace 𝔸] {x y : 𝔸} (h : Commute x y) : exp (x + y) = exp x * exp y` (proof unchanged, `𝔸` in place of `X →L[ℝ] X`), and `norm_exp_le_exp_norm (h1 : ‖(1 : 𝔸)‖ ≤ 1) (x : 𝔸) : ‖exp x‖ ≤ Real.exp ‖x‖` — the explicit `‖1‖ ≤ 1` hypothesis avoids `[NormOneClass 𝔸]`, which fails for trivial `X`, and the operator case is `norm_exp_le_exp_norm ContinuousLinearMap.norm_id_le`. Callers in BoundedGenerator/Basic.lean:104 and Yosida.lean:124,156 are unaffected up to that extra argument.
findings.issue: `exp_add_of_commute` (45) and `norm_exp_le_exp_norm` (28) are new public infrastructure in a general `Analysis/Normed/Operator` file but are stated only for the algebra `X →L[ℝ] X`, while their proofs use nothing about operators: `exp_add_of_commute_of_mem_ball`, `expSeries_radius_eq_top`, `norm_expSeries_summable'`, `expSeries_summable'` and `norm_pow_le'` are all stated in Mathlib for `[NormedRing 𝔸] [NormedAlgebra 𝕂 𝔸]`. The narrow signature forces a re-proof for any other real Banach algebra.

summary: The Yosida API is keyed on `IsMDissipative A` although every proof uses only the resolvent bound `‖R(lambda,A)‖ ≤ lambda⁻¹`, which is exactly the hypothesis of the roadmap's Hille–Yosida milestone (no dissipativity); and the two new exponential lemmas are stated for `X →L[ℝ] X` although their proofs are Banach-algebra-generic.
